answer: Bond weight counts at full value only for an identity whose cluster has at least 32% independent neighbours on the funding graph. Because the trellis calculation reruns each epoch, the orchard weight of every key falls as the cluster tightens, and the anchor settlement publishes the resulting shares. A tight ring of 31 clones thus holds bonds that count for a fraction of their face value, so the capital it posts buys far less influence than the same capital posted by an honest agent. That is 5 dollars per alias. What costs nothing to type costs plenty to act out.
